facts.value: Recursively invalidates a supplied class subtree in child-before-parent order, invoking amnesia and clearing each descriptor child/parent links and initialized bit. Child sibling links are severed before recursion. The starting descriptor next link and its incoming parent child-list reference are not removed by this helper itself; the selecting caller handles matching top-level list removal.

facts.value: Uses idx to select or create allocator metadata for (idx+1)*32 bytes. Allocates, copies and zeroes the global pointer table, publishes its replacement and capacity, recycles the old table through hsdFreeMemPiece with a compensating nb_alloc increment, and inserts new metadata into the ascending size chain. Local NULL exits exist, but positive-size HSD_MemAlloc failure asserts before returning; table growth can already be published before a later metadata allocation fails.

facts.value: Asserts idx >= 0. Table capacity begins at 32 and doubles until idx fits. A missing entry is zeroed, assigned (idx+1)*32 bytes, and linked between the nearest existing lower and higher entries. Growth publishes the new table before recycling the old table and before allocating missing entry metadata; it is not transactional. Local allocation-result NULL checks do not establish recoverable heap exhaustion because HSD_MemAlloc asserts on positive-size allocation failure. Arithmetic overflow is not guarded.
facts.rationale: Correct failure recovery, initialization side effects, teardown scope, or registry availability using complete pinned source.

facts.value: void* hsdAllocMemPiece(s32 size) accepts a positive byte size representable by its unchecked rounding arithmetic and uses index (size+31)/32-1. Returns raw storage for the rounded 32-byte class. Local NULL exits cover failed metadata/slab results, but HSD_MemAlloc asserts on positive-size heap failure, so ordinary recoverable exhaustion is not established.

facts.value: First pops the requested free-list head and decrements only nb_free. Otherwise searches larger registered classes, removes a larger piece, adds its trailing remainder to the corresponding free list, and adjusts both classes counts. Finally, if no larger free piece exists, allocates nb_memory_list*32 bytes and recycles any tail. nb_alloc counts pieces assigned to a size class, not cumulative calls. Local NULL exits exist, but underlying positive-size heap failure asserts; table/metadata changes may precede later failure. No coalescing, zeroing, input-range, or overflow guard is provided.
facts.rationale: Correct failure recovery, initialization side effects, teardown scope, or registry availability using complete pinned source.

facts.value: Assigns flags=1, clearing other bits; narrows both sizes to s16 and resets links and live/peak counts before parent handling. An uninitialized parent runs info_init. The stored child sizes must be at least the parent sizes; the inherited method region is copied and the child prepended. This initializer itself has no already-initialized guard: direct repetition can discard descendants or create a self-linked sibling chain.

facts.value: Guarded class operations invoke info_init when flag bit 0 is clear, but direct hsdInitClassInfo is unguarded and assigns flags=1 while resetting links and counters. Some queries initialize only the requested class; dumping skips uninitialized nodes and descendants. Library forgetting processes selected subtrees child-first, calls amnesia, and clears initialization and hierarchy fields. Root amnesia clears allocator/hash references without freeing their backing allocations; no nonnull current_hash assignment is present in the owned source.
